type.comment: A mutable counter, used to check handle creation and release.

methods.name: create

returnType.comment: A mutable counter, used to check handle creation and release.

methods.documentation: Creates a counter starting at the given value, or at zero by default.

methods.name: isClosed
methods.documentation: Returns true once close() has run. Only observable before the handle is released.

methods.name: getClosedCount
methods.documentation:
Total number of counters that have been released so far in this isolate.
Increments exactly once per released handle, so tests can verify that the
generated destructor ran.

methods.name: resetClosedCount
methods.documentation: Resets the released counter, so tests do not depend on execution order.

methods.documentation: Creates an instance holding the given value, or zero by default.

methods.name: addTwoNumbers
methods.documentation: A static method, so the conversion is pinned for both kinds of call.

type.comment: Bulk array operations over caller-owned buffers.

methods.name: sumFloat64
methods.documentation:
A const input buffer. Besides the const in the C header, this is what makes the
C++ generator add a std::vector<double> overload next to the raw pointer one.

methods.name: sumInt32
methods.documentation: Const on a non-double pointer, which gets the const but no vector overload.

methods.name: fillFloat64
methods.documentation: Writes value into every element of target. Checks output buffer handling.

methods.name: cumulativeSum
methods.documentation:
Writes the running total of source into target. Both buffers must hold at
least count elements. Passing the same buffer for both is supported. One const
and one mutable pointer in the same signature, so only the source picks up the
vector overload.

methods.name: reverseFloat64
methods.documentation: Reverses the buffer in place.

methods.name: dotProduct
methods.documentation: Dot product of two spans. The lengths ride along in the spans, so a mismatch is checked once here rather than in every language wrapper.

methods.name: addOffset
methods.documentation: Returns a new array with the offset added to every element. Checks a span in and an array out.

methods.name: addOffsetInt32
methods.documentation: Returns a new array with the offset added to every element. Checks an int32 span in and an array out.

methods.name: addOffsetFloat32
methods.documentation: Returns a new array with the offset added to every element. Checks a float span in and an array out.

methods.name: addOffsetUint8
methods.documentation: Returns a new array with the offset added to every element. Checks a byte span in and an array out, including embedded zeros that would truncate a string.

methods.name: getSequence
methods.documentation:
Returns 0, 1, .. count-1. A count of zero returns an empty array, and a count
over 128 forces the per-thread scratch buffer to grow, mirroring Strings.repeat.

type.comment: Synchronous callbacks into caller-provided function pointers.

methods.name: invokeTimes
methods.documentation:
Invokes the callback exactly 'times' times with indices 0 to times-1, then
returns. A null function pointer is ignored, and a non-positive count does
nothing.

methods.name: invokeOnce
methods.documentation: Invokes the callback once with the given index. Returns after it completes.

type.comment: Deliberate failures, used to check error propagation.

methods.name: requireNonNegative
methods.documentation: Throws when value is negative, otherwise does nothing.

methods.name: divideInt32
methods.documentation: Integer division. Returns 0 through the ABI when it throws.

methods.name: failingFloat64
methods.documentation: Returns 0.0 through the ABI when it throws.

methods.name: failingBool
methods.documentation: Returns false through the ABI when it throws.

methods.name: failingString
methods.documentation: Returns a null pointer through the ABI when it throws.

methods.name: failWithoutMessage
methods.documentation: Throws an exception that carries no message.

methods.name: neverThrows
methods.documentation: Marked noexcept, so no status code is generated for it.

type.comment: Index conversion for languages that count from one.

methods.name: echo
methods.documentation:
Returns the index unchanged. Both directions are marked, so a one-based caller
passes a value and gets the same value back.

methods.name: countUpTo
methods.documentation: Index in, plain number out, so only the input converts.

methods.name: lastIndexOf
methods.documentation: Plain number in, index out, so only the output converts.

methods.name: offsetFrom
methods.documentation:
Two indices that default to the first element. The default is written zero based
here and each one-based wrapper shifts it, so an omitted argument converts the
same way a supplied one does.

methods.name: fromRow
methods.documentation:
An index whose default is not zero, which is what catches a default that gets
converted twice. Omitting the argument has to reach Java as 5 in every language.

methods.name: echoSize
methods.documentation: A size_t index, so the size bridge and the index conversion have to compose.

type.comment: State confined to a second isolate.

methods.name: alwaysFails
methods.documentation: Always throws, so the secondary isolate's error path is exercised too.

type.comment: Stateless arithmetic used to check primitive type mapping.

methods.name: nextChar
methods.documentation: Returns the next UTF-16 code unit. 'A' becomes 'B'.

methods.name: addInt64
methods.documentation: Uses values above 2^32 to catch platforms that truncate long to 32 bit.

methods.name: addSize
methods.documentation: size_t in and size_t out. Bridged through int64 on the Java side.

methods.name: sizeToInt32
methods.documentation: Takes a size_t that is capped to a 32 bit Java int on the way in.

methods.name: maxInt32
methods.documentation: Returns Integer.MAX_VALUE, so callers can check the 31 bit cap.

methods.name: maxSize
methods.documentation: Returns Long.MAX_VALUE as a size_t, so callers can check the 63 bit cap.

type.comment: Default arguments and language specific convenience overloads.

methods.name: scale
methods.documentation: Both parameters have defaults, so wrappers may call this with no arguments.

methods.name: greet
methods.documentation: A trailing default only, which is the common case.

methods.name: total

cppOverloads.body: int sum = 0; for (int v : values) { sum += v; }

methods.documentation: Takes a pre-summed total. Each language gets a wrapper that sums a collection for you.

methods.name: gain
methods.documentation:
A boolean default and a double default in scientific notation. Each wrapper has
to render both in its own syntax, which is where they tend to go wrong.

methods.name: echoIndex
methods.documentation:
Returns the index unchanged. MATLAB converts to zero based indexing on the way
in and back to one based on the way out, so it sees the value it passed in.
Python clamps negatives instead, which matches C for every valid index.

methods.name: answer
methods.documentation:
The C++ wrapper body is hand written and never calls into the library, so
this is the one method where the C++ result may legitimately differ from
the others. Kept deliberately obvious.

methods.name: renamed
methods.documentation: Declared as originalName in Java but exported as renamed.

methods.name: next

returnType.comment: A named color. Values are ordinals, starting at zero.

methods.documentation: Cycles Red to Green to Blue and back to Red.

methods.name: describe
methods.documentation: Takes both enums at once, so the two generated types have to coexist in one signature.

methods.name: fromOrdinal

returnType.comment: A named color. Values are ordinals, starting at zero.

methods.documentation: Returns the enum with the given ordinal, or Red if it is out of range.

type.comment: String conversion, including non-ASCII round trips.

methods.name: echo
methods.documentation: Returns the input unchanged. Round trips UTF-8 through Java's UTF-16.

methods.name: utf8Length
methods.documentation: Length in UTF-8 bytes, which differs from the Java String length for non-ASCII input.

methods.name: utf16Length
methods.documentation: Number of UTF-16 code units, i.e. the Java String length.

methods.name: empty
methods.documentation: Returns an empty string, which must not be confused with a null pointer.

methods.name: nullString
methods.documentation: Returns a null pointer rather than an empty string.

methods.name: join
methods.documentation: Joins a char* array with a separator. Checks const char** parameter handling.

methods.name: repeat
methods.documentation: Returns a string longer than the initial scratch buffer, forcing it to grow.

type.comment: Reads fields out of a caller-owned struct.

methods.name: totalPower
methods.documentation:
Power draw in watts for the given current. Returns zero unless the actuator is
enabled and in the running state (2), so all three fields decide the result.

methods.name: checkedVoltage
methods.documentation: Bus voltage in volts. Returns 0.0 through the ABI when it throws.

methods.name: getStatus

returnType.comment: Status reading for the given index.

methods.documentation:
Fills the out parameter with a canned reading for the given index: index 0
reads (48.0, running, enabled), every other index reads (12.5, 1, disabled).

methods.name: getCheckedStatus
methods.documentation: Same readings as getStatus. Every field of the out parameter reads as zero through the ABI when it throws.

structs.name: ByteSpan
structs.comment:
A (pointer, length) view of a contiguous byte buffer, passed and returned
by value. Binary data rather than a string: embedded zeros are data.
Inputs are caller-owned and only read during the call. Returned spans are
library-owned and stay valid until the calling thread's next library call,
so they have to be copied immediately.

structs.name: DoubleSpan
structs.comment:
A (pointer, length) view of a contiguous double buffer, passed and returned

spans are library-owned and stay valid until the calling thread's next
library call, so they have to be copied immediately.
